Direction: host->client.

host -> client. A message was ignored; diagnostic only, never changes match state.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refSeq` | integer | yes | The seq of the message being rejected. |
| `refType` | string | yes |  |
| `code` | `"not_grant_holder"` \| `"stale_grant"` \| `"bad_signature"` \| `"unexpected_state"` \| `"schema"` \| `"unknown_player"` | yes |  |
| `message` | string | yes |  |

### `RECONNECT`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host. First frame on a new socket to the current host, after a drop or a host transfer; never a fresh HELLO.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `player` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) | yes | Who is resuming; must equal the envelope from. |
| `logHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | Hash of the last log entry this participant holds; 64 zeros when it holds none. |
| `logLength` | integer | yes |  |
| `signature` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$`) | yes | The participant's signature over canonicalJson({matchId, player, logHash, logLength}) with its roster key. In a lobby (A17; `match` is present) it is over canonicalJson({lobby, host, player, match, logHash, logLength, seq}): the lobby's code, the player id of the lobby's PC the frame is sent to, the same `match` as below, and the envelope's own `seq`: the frame is good for one use, at the PC it was written for. |
| `resends` | boolean | no | A18: true when the sender sends again, right after an accepted RECONNECT, its own BALL_END, GAME_OVER, FORFEIT and LOG_SIGN that the host never answered. Absent or false: it does not, and a ball end it reported into the dropped link comes back only for a grant the host issues again (after a PAUSE and its RESUME). |
| `match` | string \| null | no | A17: the match the sender holds a log of; null: none. Absent: a RECONNECT from before the lobby, whose envelope names the match. |

### `RECONNECT_ACK`

Direction: host->client.

host -> client. Answers RECONNECT. A rejected client must re-join with a fresh HELLO; the host closes the socket after a rejection.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accept` | boolean | yes |  |
| `code` | `"unknown_log_hash"` \| `"unknown_player"` \| `"bad_signature"` \| `"match_not_started"` \| `"protocol_version"` \| `"stale_seq"` \| null | yes | Why the RECONNECT was rejected; null when accepted. A17: `protocol_version`: the sender speaks another version; `stale_seq`: the envelope's `seq` is not above the last this host took from that member (a RECONNECT sent a second time). In a lobby `unknown_player` means the member's place is gone: it joins again with a fresh HELLO, the first frame of a new link. |
| `entries` | array of object | yes | Every log entry after the one the client named, in order; empty when it is current or rejected. |
| `logHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | The host's log head after these entries. In a lobby's answer: the head of the log the answer carries (with `more`, at the end of this first page; for a `restart` or a refusal, which carry no log, 64 zeros and length 0). |
| `logLength` | integer | yes |  |
| `match` | string \| null | no | A17: the match that is open now; null: none. Absent: not said (no lobby). |
| `restart` | boolean | no | A17: true: the sender's log is not of the open match (or none is open): drop it. The open match's log follows in MATCH_LOG. Absent: false. |
| `more` | boolean | no | A17: true: `entries` holds only the first page (at most 100); the rest follows in MATCH_LOG, and the sender is current at its last page. Absent: false. |
| `closed` | boolean | no | A17: true: the match the sender holds a log of (`RECONNECT.match`) ended while it was away, and is the last one the lobby closed: `entries` (and MATCH_LOG, with `more`) bring that log to its end, then that match's RESULTs and its MATCH_END follow as they were sent, and after them the lobby as it is now (the open match's log, if one is open, from entry 0). Nothing is reported into the closed match again. Absent: false. |
| `seqAbove` | integer | no | A17: with `stale_seq`: the last `seq` the lobby took from this member. The member's next RECONNECT carries a `seq` above it (signed, as every one is), so a counter that fell behind is no reason to stay out, and the counter itself is never moved back. |

### `MEDIA_SIGNAL`

Direction: any.

any -> `to`, through the host: it forwards the frame to `to` only, `from` preserved. Sets up the peer-to-peer video and voice between two participants; never logged, never trusted for anything but media.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) | yes | The one participant this signal is for. The host forwards it there and nowhere else. |
| `kind` | `"offer"` \| `"answer"` \| `"ice"` \| `"reset"` \| `"stereo"` | yes | An SDP offer or answer, or one ICE candidate. `reset`: the sender's connections to `to` are new (its panel was rebuilt); close yours and negotiate afresh. `stereo`: what the sender's video is (VPX's VR preview on one eye or both). |
| `sdp` | string | no | The session description; present on offer and answer. |
| `candidate` | object | no | Present on ice. |
| `stereo` | `"mono"` \| `"sbs"` \| null | no | Present on stereo: `sbs` = left eye \| right eye side by side, `mono` = one picture, null = the sender does not know (the receiver guesses from the picture's shape). |
| `eyes` | array of object \| null | no | Optional on stereo `sbs`: the geometry of [left, right] as the sender rendered them (the OpenXR layer camera, D7.5). Absent or null: a screen capture; the receiver assumes its own eyes. |
| `channel` | `"rtc"` \| `"video"` \| `"stream"` | yes | Which peer connection between the two the signal belongs to: `rtc` (absent = `rtc`), the Electron connection that carries voice (and video until D10.7); `video`, the native video helper's connection for the same pair (castcade-video.exe, D10); `stream` (protocol 6), the data-only connection that carries the VPX state stream between the two companions (a waiting player watches the player up on their own table, I11.4.2). A peer that does not run the helper ignores `video` signals; every peer opens the `stream` connection, whether or not its VPX can use it. |

### `PARTICIPANT_UPDATE`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host in the lobby: replaces the sender's HELLO `participant.rig` and `game`; the host compares the fingerprint again and re-sends HELLO_ACK to every client; (I11.4.9) `stream3dWaitMs` says whether the sender's 3D connection is still being made. After MATCH_READY (A6.1, 2026-11-01) only `rig`, (B26) `advisory` and (B26.4) `midnightMode` count: the roster in the log stays final, and the host passes the update on to every other participant (`from` preserved) and sends its own the same way, so each Match tab and panel shows the rig each player has now. Never logged. In a lobby (A17) it counts in every phase for `rig`, `game`, `ballEndReady`, `midnightMode`, `stance`, `noCopy` and `ownGame`: the host answers with HELLO_ACK to every member, and a match's logged roster and fingerprint stay what its MATCH_READY said.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rig` | `"pc"` \| `"vr_headset"` \| `"real_cabinet"` | no | The sender's rig now, when it changed since HELLO. |
| `game` | object | no | The sender's fingerprint now, when its table changed since HELLO. |
| `ballEndReady` | boolean | no | A13: whether the sender's table can report ball ends now (see `HELLO.ballEndReady`), when that changed since HELLO. Lobby only. |
| `advisory` | object | no | B26: after MATCH_READY only: a flag about one of the sender's own balls (see `PlayerAdvisory`). The host passes the update on to every other participant like a rig change (`from` preserved) and sends its own the same way. A peer from before B26 ignores it. |
| `midnightMode` | object | no | B26.4: the Midnight Madness setting on the sender's table (see `MidnightMode`), when its companion could read it, in any phase. In the lobby the host lists it in HELLO_ACK `midnightModes`; after MATCH_READY it passes the update on like a rig change. A peer from before B26.4 ignores it. |
| `stream3dWaitMs` | integer | no | I11.4.9: lobby only: the sender's PC is still making its 3D connection (its VPX build has not connected to its Castcade yet, or nothing has been heard from another player's PC over the state stream's data connection), and stops waiting for it in at most this many ms; 0: settled (or given up). The host lists it in HELLO_ACK `stream3dWait` and holds a start from its table meanwhile. Absent: no change. A peer from before I11.4.9 ignores it. |
| `stance` | `"play"` \| `"watch"` | no | A17: the sender's choice now, Play or Watch at the next start. It changes nothing in a game that is being played. |
| `noCopy` | boolean | no | A17: true: the sender's PC has no copy of the lobby's table (`HELLO_ACK.hostGame`); false: it has. |
| `ownGame` | boolean | no | A17: true: a game the match does not own is running on the sender's table (played alone, in the lobby or as a watcher); false: it has ended. |

### `NEXT_GAME`

Direction: host->all.

host -> all, logged. Only after the previous game's RESULT went out. Every listed player starts a fresh game: grant 1 follows, ball counts and scores start again.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `game` | integer | yes | The game that starts now: the previous one plus 1. |
| `playerOrder` | array of string (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) | yes | Who plays this game, in rotation order: the roster's players still connected, the host first (its table started the game). A player who left is out of this game and its standings. |

### `MATCH_END`

Direction: host->all.

host -> all, between games: the series is over; the last RESULT stands. Never logged; the host closes the match afterwards. In a lobby (A17) it means "this match is over, back to the lobby": nobody leaves, no connection closes, and the next match starts a log of its own.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `games` | integer | yes | How many games of the match have a RESULT. |
| `reason` | string | yes |  |
| `abandoned` | integer \| null | no | A17: the game that was being played and was ended for everyone: no RESULT, a win for nobody. Null or absent: none. |

### `START_REQUEST`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host, in a lobby. A member asks for a start. The host announces it (HELLO_ACK `start`) or answers REJECT (`unexpected_state`) whose `message` is the sentence the asker is shown.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fromTable` | boolean | yes | True: the sender's own game began on its table (A11). Taken from the starter only. |
| `newMatch` | boolean | yes | True: end the open match and start one with everyone set to Play (the explicit press, never set with `fromTable`). |
| `anyway` | boolean | yes | A13: the sender confirmed a start with a table that cannot report ball ends. |
| `now` | boolean | yes | Do not wait: start without the 3D connections and without the people whose table is not ready (a second press). |

### `START_CANCEL`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host, in a lobby. Take back the start that counts down or waits; answered by the HELLO_ACK without it, or by REJECT.

_No fields._

### `END_REQUEST`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host, in a lobby, between games. End the open match; answered by MATCH_END, or by REJECT.

_No fields._

### `TABLE_PICK`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host, in a lobby, outside a game. A member picks the lobby's table; answered by the HELLO_ACK that carries it (`hostGame`, `tablePickedBy`), or by REJECT.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `game` | object | yes | The picked table: its identity keys (`kind`, `tableName`, `tableHash`, `romName`); the other keys are facts of one PC's copy and are null or empty in a pick. |

### `LOBBY_CLOSED`

Direction: host->all.

host -> all. The lobby is closed: every member tears down, and nobody reconnects afterwards. Never logged.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes |  |

### `MATCH_LOG`

Direction: host->client.

host -> client, in a lobby. The open match's log, to a member who does not hold it (it joined while the match was open, or its RECONNECT_ACK said `more`), in pages. The host sends such a member no logged message until the last page went out. Never logged.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match` | string | yes | The match the entries belong to. |
| `restart` | boolean | yes | True on the first page of a whole log: the receiver starts an empty log for `match`. False: the entries follow the ones the receiver holds. |
| `entries` | array of object | yes | The next entries of the log, in order, verbatim. |
| `logHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | The head of the log at the end of this page: the receiver's head once it has appended the entries (64 zeros for an empty log). Every page names the head of the log it carries. |
| `logLength` | integer | yes |  |
| `more` | boolean | yes | Another page follows. False: the receiver is current, and the logged messages reach it live from here on. |

### `LEAVE_LOBBY`

Direction: client->host.

client -> host, in a lobby. The sender leaves on purpose: its row goes at once (a game it is playing it gives up first), a start it was in is looked at again, and its place is free. Sent before the link closes; nothing answers it but the HELLO_ACK the others get. Never logged.

_No fields._

## Shared objects

### `GameFingerprint`

Everything that must match between participants for a fair match. The host compares these at HELLO.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"vpx"` \| `"arcade"` | yes | Emulator family. |
| `tableName` | string | yes | Human name of the table or ROM set. |
| `tableHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | SHA-256 of the ORIGINAL .vpx (never the patched copy), or of the arcade ROM zip. |
| `romName` | string \| null | yes | PinMAME ROM set name (e.g. mm_109c) or arcade ROM name; null for originals. |
| `romHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) \| null | yes | SHA-256 of the ROM zip; null for originals. |
| `physicsHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) \| null | yes | Hash of the physics-relevant table settings; null when not computed. |
| `recipeVersion` | string \| null | yes | Castcade patch recipe version applied to this table (ADR 0004); null for arcade. |
| `sidecarHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) \| null | yes | SHA-256 of the generated sidecar .vbs; proves both players run the same patch. |
| `emulatorVersion` | string | yes | VPX or RetroArch core version string. |

### `ParticipantInfo`



| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `playerId` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) | yes | Stable participant id for this match: the ArcAid user id, or a fakeclient label. |
| `displayName` | string | yes |  |
| `publicKey` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$`) | yes | Ed25519 public key, 32 raw bytes, base64. |
| `rig` | `"pc"` \| `"vr_headset"` \| `"real_cabinet"` | yes | The player's declared rig, for provenance (ArcAid badge, never a gate). |

### `GrantBody`

The signed part of a TURN_GRANT. Signature is over canonicalJson(GrantBody).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `matchId` | string | yes | The Throwdown code from ArcAid, or any unique string in a local/fake match. |
| `player` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) | yes | Who may play. |
| `ballNumber` | integer | yes | Which ball of their game this grant covers. |
| `grantSeq` | integer | yes | Monotonic per match; a client ignores a grant with a lower seq than one it has seen. |
| `issuedAt` | integer | yes | Host clock, ms since epoch. |
| `logHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | Hash of the host log head when the grant was issued; lets a client detect a forked log. |
| `game` | integer | no | Which game of the series this grant belongs to (1-based; protocol 3 hosts always send it). |

### `LogEntry`

One entry of the hash-chained match log, exactly as every participant holds it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer | yes |  |
| `prevHash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | Hash of the previous entry; 64 zeros before the first. |
| `ts` | integer | yes | The causing message's own ts, never a local clock. |
| `kind` | `"msg"` \| `"grant"` \| `"event"` | yes |  |
| `from` | string (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) | yes | Stable participant id for this match: the ArcAid user id, or a fakeclient label. |
| `message` | object | no | The logged envelope, verbatim; absent on an event entry. |
| `event` | object | no | Present only when kind is event. |
| `hash` | string (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) | yes | sha256(canonicalJson(entry without hash)). |
